bibliography.note: Johnson, Timothy B. & Evans, David O. 1990 (March). Size-dependent winter mortality of young-of-the-year white perch: climate warming and invasion of the Laurentian Great Lakes. Transactions of the American Fisheries Society 119(2): 301–313. show.mjs reported 'DOI NOT FOUND' only because it cut the DOI at its '(' — the full DOI resolves at Crossref. The ledger's parenthesis says 'fed and starved, at 2.5 and 4 °C'; the abstract mentions feeding only for the 4.0 °C trials.

claims.claim: laboratory, 4.0 °C, starved 180 d: 40.6 % died (none when fed); mortality highest in the smallest
laboratory, 2.5 °C, 150 d: 68.4–71.2 % died; yellow perch 0.8 % (Johnson & Evans 1990, 1991, abstracts)
the white perch's first winter runs on Johnson & Evans's (1990) measured model
field young perch live on their autumn lipid, so first-winter mortality is size-selective (Post & Evans 1989; Johnson & Evans 1990, 1991)
YOY held at 4.0 °C, starved or fed: fed 0 % dead, starved 40.6 % at 180 d; p = min(1, A·e^(B·WD − C·FL)) with A 7.29543, B 0.02145, C 0.10804, WD the days at 4 °C, FL fork length (mm)
at Hot Brook's ~161 days below 4 °C: all starved fish < 50 mm FL die, half at 57 mm, a tenth at 72 mm (project arithmetic)
claims.note: Arithmetic on the abstract's formula holds: ln 7.29543 + 0.02145·161 = 5.440, so p = 1 at FL 50.4, 0.5 at 56.8, 0.1 at 71.7 mm. But FL's unit (mm) and p as a proportion (not a percent) are the project's inference (first_winter_mortality.md §2), not read in the paper.

notes: Blocked: the full text is paywalled (OUP/Wiley) and no open or archived copy was found; the paper itself already labels this row '(abstract)'. What the abstract (OpenAlex) says, for whoever opens the article: YOY tested at constant 2.5 and 4.0 °C; 'At 4.0°C, mortality was high for the smallest fish when food was withheld, but no mortality occurred under ad libitum feeding'; 40.6 % of starved fish died over 180 d at 4.0 °C; PMORT = 7.29543·e^(0.02145·WD − 0.10804·FL) at 4.0 °C, WD being 'the number of days' exposure to 4.0 or 2.5°C'; at 2.5 °C 68.4 % died after 150 d, PMORT = 0.28054·e^(0.01862·WD − 0.03097·FL). So the code's A, B and C match the abstract's 4.0 °C model, and Table 3.6-9's first row matches it. Not in the 1990 abstract: the 71.2 % and the yellow perch 0.8 % (presumably Johnson & Evans 1991, CJFAS 48:672–680, its own entry), whether the 2.5 °C fish were fed, the sizes tested, and FL's unit. Things to check in the full text: FL in mm vs cm and PMORT as proportion vs percent (the project's reading reproduces 40.6 % at a mean FL of ~62.5 mm); the size range tested (the code applies the model down to FL < 50 mm); and whether a constant-4.0 °C model fits 'days below 4 °C' in the field, where under-ice water is often 1–3 °C and the 2.5 °C model is far harsher (at WD 161 it kills 64 % at FL 70 mm and 25 % at 100 mm, per first_winter_mortality.md).
